baseball_review: Kurtz has 50 A/AA PA, four HR and a .63 preseason rank score, yet p is 6.06 percent and c 168.16. Workload and absent listing pull down the saved head; zero refined active analogues qualify the extrapolation. All reported quantiles are zero because the nonappearance mass exceeds 90 percent, not because batting talent is zero. Actual 489 PA is a readiness miss; generic zero-PA peers do not make it reasonable or fixable through spread alone.

Langford has 200 professional PA and ten HR with AA/AAA exposure and .95 rank. Rank adds 147.25 active PA along saved paths; no current MLB workload subtracts 94.00. p 59.91 percent and c 358.74 leave the mean low. New P90 523 is closer to 557 than narrow 372/forest 238, but still misses. Earlier refined active support is zero; Crews's 132 and the other controls' zero outcomes show timing variation, not elite-specific validation.

Alonso's 574 AA/AAA PA and 36 HR are present, with .50 rank. Minor games and AA exposure yield 80.36 percent arrival, but c remains 267.58 due partly to absent MLB workload. New P90 459 improves on 283/323, still well below actual 693. Five refined active analogues and similar-workload unsuccessful peers are not equivalent productive 36-HR bats; wider risk does not repair the active-workload mean.

Judge after 2016 retains 95 MLB PA and 410 AAA PA with 19 AAA HR. Listing and games favor 92.50 percent appearance; ranks add active workload while brief MLB sample reduces it, ending at c 335.05. New range 56-561 scores better than both references but actual 678 is still outside. Four refined active matches and mixed Renfroe/Moya/Waldrop/Hernandez timing qualify the immediate opportunity claim; no future hitting-breakout claim follows.

Judge after 2024 has three MLB seasons of 696/458/704 PA and 62/37/58 HR. The saved head gives 99.07 percent appearance but only c 535.74; age reduces active workload while current workload increases it. New 315-720 range contains actual 679, yet older forest quantile loss 13.03 beats new 34.67 because its median is closer. A large broad profile count does not validate star workload; this is a retained harm against the stronger reference.

McLain after 2024 has no current PA but 403 prior MLB PA and 16 HR. Listing=0 conflicts with reviewed October activation provenance and remains unchanged. Workload subtracts 93.05 active PA; prior quality/role help. p 44.67 percent times c 294.75 gives 131.65 expected PA; new P90 414 improves on 305/344 but misses actual 577. Eight active matches and legal/marginal peers do not establish medical-return support.

Belt's good 404-PA, 19-HR season remains positive evidence; he was unsigned, not known retired. Listing absence reduces log odds, but games/quality yield p 64.63 percent and c 377.77. New range includes zero and scores better than both references before actual zero, without claiming prescience. Martinez/Blackmon/McCutchen/Canha all returned; this remains a reasonable unusual miss, not permission to zero all older free agents.

Franco after 2023 has strong MLB workload and listing=1, which push p to 99.05 percent; the current statistical heads omit the relevant administrative-availability state. c 564.86 and new P10 350 still miss actual zero. New quantile loss beats narrow but loses to forest. The peers are active shortstops, not legal controls. Wrong nonappearance mass is an availability representation gap; positive spread cannot solve it or imply poor hitting talent.

Lowrie after 2018 has 680 PA and 23 HR; games lift p to 90.65 percent despite listing absence, while age reduces active workload to c 505.98. Actual eight PA is a positive-tail rather than zero-appearance miss. New P10 111 improves on narrow 472, giving the largest narrow-reference gain, but forest P10 82/loss129.50 still beats new loss135.73. This supports broadening against a weak baseline, not a proved injury model.

Hoskins has no 2023 PA after 672 PA and 30 HR. His p 10.07 percent is barely above the 10 percent threshold, so unconditional P90 maps to about the active distribution's 0.65th percentile. Broader positive spread therefore lowers P90 from narrow 228 to sixteen rather than necessarily raising it. Actual 517 produces the largest harm against both references. Prior regular talent/medical return is not captured by broad zero-PA peers; wrong return probability is the substantive gap.

Ortiz retains productive 626-PA, 38-HR history, with raw active PA 504.66 and a raw participation head that does not enforce retirement. The preexisting reported-retirement wrapper sets p=0; new and narrow laws both forecast zero, correctly. The largest forest gain is existing context, not new dispersion. Applying the same origin-known retirement/permanent policy to fifteen reference rows removes 9.68 percent of the overall advantage; other reference mean/feature differences remain.

McLain after 2023 has 403 MLB PA with 16 HR and strong AAA production. Listing/games/quality give p 98.53 percent and c 608.34; expected599.38 is the largest false high before next-year zero PA. New lower quantile399 is lower than narrow592 but still misses, and forest scores better. The later injury cannot be inserted into the earlier forecast. Broad earlier support does not provide full-season availability protection; individual surprise is not itself proof of an unreasonable mean.

Tatis after 2022 has no current MLB PA but 546 PA and 42 HR in 2021 plus shortened 2020 production. Restricted-list/finite-suspension context is not permanent retirement; current listing zero and empty workload leave p 13.40 percent and c 296.16. New P90 174 is worse than narrow 287/forest 472 before 635 actual. Generic sparse-window peers are not prior MLB stars. The temporary absence/return representation and probability remain wrong; global positive spread cannot fix this largest false low.

Engel after 2021 has 140 MLB PA with seven HR and 60 AAA PA; the earlier shortened 2020 MLB sample is not interpreted as a full schedule. Listing/games/quality yield p 94.24 percent and c 275.86; expected 259.97 is nearly exact before 260 actual. New quantile loss 17.47 beats forest 26.57 but loses to narrow 3.83 for this realization. The selected peers include Trout, an imperfect talent match; one accurate mean is not proof of low true risk or a reason to retune dispersion.
